topic: anonymity and the deindividuation effect (1969 hooded-shock study)
title: Anonymity Doesn't Reveal You — It Changes You
description: The psychology of anonymity: why hiding your identity doesn't just show your "true self," it can actually change how you act. A quick look at the deindividuation effect and a real 1969 experiment. AI-narrated commentary — original take, not a summary of any single source video.

hook_candidates.text: Anonymity doesn't just reveal who you are — it can change who's behind the mask.
In 1969, a psychologist found anonymous people acted far more aggressively than identified ones.
Why do decent people say things online they'd never say to your face?
A psychologist hid people's faces behind hoods, then watched what they did when no one could tell it was them.
